maya: Heads up — ran the AWQ/INT8 bake with prefix cache + continuous batching on llm-70b. Seeing a consistent quality regression on long-prefix prompts. anyone else hit this?
sanjay: oof, can you share numbers?
maya: MMLU microavg dropped from 81.2% -> 79.4% (~1.8% abs). Perplexity on WikiText val went from 12.4 -> 14.2. Latency improved ~18% and throughput +32%, so it's not totally free.
eli: interesting. which quant path? AWQ int8 only? FP8? GPTQ mix?
maya: AWQ-int8 primarily. Also tried GPTQ-4bit and FP8 on a subset — regression only shows up when prefix cache is enabled AND continuous batching is on. If either is off, quality matches baseline.
olivia: could be stale KV reuse or hash collisions when keys get quantized? We changed key packing in AWQ earlier.
elsn: (typo) eli: hah — scalar mismatch in cache key generation could cause wrong pasts to be used. Any diffs in cache key bytes between int8/float runs?
maya: did a quick diff: when cache keys are generated post-quantization we see 0.2% of keys changed due to rounding differences -> not huge but maybe amplified by prefix length. KV hit rate also drops: 72% -> 58% when continuous batching merges requests.
sanjay: that drop is suspect. Continuous batching merges different prefix lengths and we do key normalization in the runtime. If quantized model uses different key hashing (e.g., float32 -> int8 packing), collisions might increase.
maya: exact repro command I used:
```
python -m infra.run_eval --model=llm-70b --quant=awq-int8 --cache=prefix --batching=continuous --dataset=mmlu,wikitext --seed=42 --batch-window-ms=30
```
maya: runtime config snippet:
```
model:
  name: "llm-70b-awq"
  quant: "awq-int8"
  kvcache:
    enabled: true
    prefix_sharing: true
    normalize_keys: true
    key_hash: "sha256"
batching:
  mode: continuous
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_latency_ms: 50
```
maya: bench-bot reported the metric breakdown: throughput +32%, p95 latency -15%, but MMLU -1.8%.
bench-bot: MMLU: baseline 81.2 -> awq-int8+cache 79.4, perp: 12.4 -> 14.2, kv_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.58, tokens/sec: 1220 -> 1608.
eli: can you try disabling prefix_sharing and leave normalize_keys on? If prefix_sharing merges keys aggressively that could cause partial past reuse.
maya: tried that — disabling prefix_sharing recovered ~0.9% of the drop (so still ~0.9% remaining).
sanjay: next suspicion: ordering of quantization + key serialization. If we quantize activations and then serialize float-based keys, slight bit differences could flip hashes. We should canonicalize to pre-quantized float representation for keygen.
maya: agreed. I hacked runtime locally to compute kvcache keys using float32 pre-quant values and that eliminated almost all mismatches. Need a clean patch though.
olivia: important to evaluate rollout risk. For Dedicated/Dynamic pools we could disable prefix cache by default for AWQ-int8 models until patch lands. For hosted users we might auto-fallback.
deploy-bot: note created: rollout-ticket#ML-1128 (disable prefix cache for awq-int8 on hosted until keyfix). linked to infra-2345.
eli: experimental patch idea: add feature flag `kvcache.key_source = pre_quant` and `kvcache.disable_on_quantized=true` to config. Then we can A/B traffic.
maya: quick perf delta for that approach: turning key_source=pre_quant recovers accuracy to 81.0 (so still -0.2), throughput stays +25% (slightly lower than before). Worth it.
sanjay: can you instrument a new metric: collisions_per_1k_keys and avg_prefix_length_on_miss. Add to rollout dashboard.
maya: will add. Also noticed GPTQ-4bit didn't show same hit; seems this is specific to AWQ packing algorithm.
eli: ok next steps: maya to push kvcache key-source patch + test, sanjay to add collisions metric and dashboard, olivia to prepare a short rollback/playbook if we disable prefix cache in hosted.
maya: posting PR draft in ~30m. thanks. :thumbsup:
olivia: thanks — nice catch.
bench-bot: PR lint OK, perf tests queued.
